This scale sits in the codebook's legacy-items tables rather than the PROMIS bank sections, so it has its own re-derivation script. All 20 items share one response set, which rederive_cesd.py asserts. Independent corroboration of the code-to-text tie, using the data rather than the codebook: the canonical CES-D words items 4, 8, 12 and 16 positively and the other 16 negatively, the shipped stems put the positive wording at exactly those four numbers ('I felt that I was just as good as other people', 'I felt hopeful about the future', 'I was happy', 'I enjoyed life'), and in the live data those four are the only items that correlate negatively with the rest -- mean r against the other 19 of -0.29 to -0.13 against +0.22 to +0.34 for all sixteen others, with no overlap between the two groups. The shared instruction sentence is carried in instructions; the codebook gives no separate item context, so section_prompt is empty.

Every live resp level in all eight tables maps onto a position in its own item's ladder, with no level left over. The survey ran in 47 languages across 179 countries, so no single administered language exists to name; the shipped text is the English master form and the language column is omitted rather than given a value wrong for most respondents. Raised on #1831 as a case #1777 does not cover.

Every item code in all eleven tables is a column of that file, which rederive_ecps.py re-checks. The exception is ecps_sahm_2024_emotion, which genuinely is the ERQ short form: COVIDiSTRESS II included it as a block, and that is the subsample Sahm et al. validated. Item text is tied to item codes by the instrument's listing order within each block, with block item counts matching the live tables exactly. The identity block lists 4 statements and the table has 4 items. The wording is corroborated by a second document: the block appears in both workbooks and their 5 lines agree word for word. OPTION LABELS COME FROM THE ADMINISTERED FORM, not the questionnaire workbooks. The two workbooks on OSF are registration-stage documents and their response designs do not describe what was administered: they give information acquisition as a 1-7 slider where the data run 1-10, and the agreement scales as 1-6 where the data run 1-7 or 0-6. 'Copy of survey.pdf', in the Round II project's own Final Data Set folder, is the Qualtrics form and prints every ladder verbatim. It settled two things the workbooks got wrong: the agreement ladder carries a NEUTRAL midpoint the workbooks omitted, so a six-anchor list is really seven options; and the compliance items are past tense. Every live resp level in all eight tables maps onto a position in its own item's ladder, with no level left over. The form is authoritative but its print view is partial -- it renders one statement per randomised misperception block and two rows of each norm matrix -- so 190 shipped strings verify against it and 16 against the workbooks, 0 against neither, which rederive_ecps.py reports per run. Positions the form left without a verbal label ship empty rather than invented. Trust is the one block here that is not an agreement scale: the form prints it as a percentage slider running 'No trust' then 10% through 90% in ten-point steps, which is exactly the live 0-10 range, 11 positions. The top position's label is not in the PDF's text layer, so resp 10 ships empty rather than inferred as 100%; 70 of the 77 option cells are labelled. This block has no _0neutral twin in the cleaned file and needs none, its codes being plain trust_1 to trust_7. The survey ran in 47 languages across 179 countries, so no single administered language exists to name; the shipped text is the English master form and the language column is omitted rather than given a value wrong for most respondents. Raised on #1831 as a case #1777 does not cover.
